newsitem.title: USA: Argentina sees talks on new IMF program in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Argentina sees talks on new IMF program in Dec.

text.p: Argentina expects to open talks on an extended fund facility with the International Monetary Fund in December, Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said Sunday.
Fernandez told a news conference that the IMF mission would visit Buenos Aires at the end of the year.
According to Fernandez, the new program could help support the labor and health care reforms Argentina plans to undertake in the near future.
Argentina also expects the IMF to approve a $1.2 billion standby loan in October, Fernandez said.
Argentina revised some of its economic targets for 1996 and projections for 1997 to secure the IMF's support for the standby agreement originally granted earlier this year.
Fernandez singled out a Gross Domestic Product increase of five percent for 1997 as an important goal of the letter of intent submitted to the IMF.
According to IMF estimates, Argentina is slated to finish 1996 with a 2.5 percent growth of GDP, rebounding from a 4.4 percent contraction in 1995.
